mathematics.summary: An actual original-coordinate carrier with four square-Gram modes at scale g and global s3(A)>=s has a quantitative density bound. Exhaustive branches: three self modes -> finite core; approximate rank two self -> physical pair; small self norm -> literal rank-three crossing; rank-one self survivor -> original scalar pivot, Schur shear, rank-two crossing, half-Riesz square peel. Arbitrary added spectrum remains inside the final matrix.
mathematics.new_key_inequality: In the rank-one self survivor, after choosing a physical pivot and Schur shear, s2(Bprime) >= ell(L)*s3(B), so four square modes leave two literal crossing directions after one scalar peel.
mathematics.continuity: continuous C0 only on rank-three crossing branch; essential boundedness for combined theorem

partner.application: For A0^2=4I on an 8-coordinate carrier, p=2 commuting severe losses, q=1 noncommuting destructive-square defect budget, r=1 arbitrary rank packet and ||T||<=1/4 give sqrt(lambda4((A^2)_H))>=7/4 and globally s3(A)>=7/4. The new four-mode compiler then gives density <4094 with explicit rational parameters.
